Title: Original Post Oak BBQ Sauce
Description:
This is the sauce we started with, back when the creek kept us home. Tomato and cider vinegar up front, a real hit of coarse black pepper, and just enough brown sugar to round off the edges. We steep a split of post oak in every batch, so it tastes like the pit instead of a bottle of liquid smoke.

It's thin on purpose. Central Texas sauce should slide into sliced brisket, not sit on top of it.

  • Size: 12 fl oz (355 mL) or 18 fl oz (532 mL) glass bottle
  • Pairs with: Sliced brisket, smoked sausage, turkey breast, a breakfast taco the morning after
  • Storage and care: Shelf-stable until opened. Refrigerate after opening and use within 3 months.

Ingredients: Tomato paste, apple cider vinegar, water, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce (distilled vinegar, molasses, sugar, water, salt, onions, anchovies, garlic, cloves, tamarind extract, natural flavorings, chili pepper extract), coarse black pepper, sea salt, dried onion, dried garlic, ancho chile powder, post oak smoke.

Drizzle it on fried chicken, pepperoni pizza, cornbread or a slab of smoked pork belly. It also works in a glaze: equal parts hot honey and Original sauce.

Central Texas brisket is salt and pepper, and we didn't mess with that. We sized the pepper right (16-mesh, the coarse grind pitmasters argue about), balanced it with kosher salt, and added a little granulated garlic and onion so the bark tastes finished.

Use about a tablespoon per pound. It does the same job on beef ribs, a thick ribeye or a pot of chili.

No sugar, no MSG, no anti-caking agents.
